text:
jin: Heads-up, ran onboarding eval for the new tiny-multilang model (v2-mini) after q4_0 quant. Seeing weird token collapse on vertical CJK inputs (OCR-like, lots of explicit newlines).
jin: Baseline fp16 model handles it fine; q4_0 output drops line breaks and sometimes merges graphemes -> downstream BLEU/chrF drop.
jin: minimal repro:
```
# input (visual lines)
漢
字
テスト
# tokenizer.encode shows: ['漢字テスト'] on q4 bits vs ['漢','\n','字','\n','テスト'] on fp16
```
maya: yikes. do you have the exact tokenizer config used for quant build? was any pre-normalization step added when we fused kernels?
jin: same tokenizer.json, but our quant inference path applies a small normalization pass (NFKC + strip_bidi) to reduce cache keys. suspect strip_bidi is overzealous.
sam: I remember the kernel fusion pass also removed explicit ZWJ/ZWNJ preservation to squeeze token map size. could be bitpacking change.
harpreet: eval-bot posted batch metrics — chrF delta looks bad on vertical set: -6.4 overall, but for Japanese vertical subset -12.1. Arabic/RTL set has punctuation ordering errors after quant too.
eval-bot: metrics snapshot: {"baseline_fp16": "chrF 52.3", "q4_0": "chrF 45.9", "delta": "-6.4"} (posted to /evals/feeds).
maya: quick triage plan: 1) rerun tokenizer with preserve_newlines flag, 2) run quant inference with bidi preservation enabled, 3) bisect whether kernel fusion or post-token normalize is the culprit.
jin: ran step 1 locally: preserve_newlines restores tokens but q4_0 model still sometimes emits merged graphemes when input uses U+200D/ZWJ sequences (honorifics in korean). small sample:
```
input: 김
씨 (ZWJ between syllables)
fp16 tokens: ['김','\u200D','씨']
q4_0 tokens: ['김씨']
```
sam: that's indicative of the token map being rebuilt with a dedupe that treats ZWJ as non-significant. pushing a test to kernel branch that keeps zero-width joiners intact.
harpreet: FYI, Arabic bidi issues seem to come from a normalization pass that reorders punctuation before tokenization; with q4 rounding the model loses context tokens and re-rendering order is off.
maya: can we get a small eval harness: run the same prompt through fp16, int8, q4_0 with identical tokenization (explicitly force our tokenizer binary) and capture token streams + model logits for first 8 steps? that will tell if loss of tokens is pre-tokenizer or during KV/cache flow.
jin: already capturing logs — attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-14T15:02:11Z INFO tokenizer: preserve_newlines=true, keep_zwj=true
2026-03-14T15:02:11Z INFO model.q4_0: batch=1 seq=128 kernel=optimized-v2 kv-cache=enabled
2026-03-14T15:02:12Z WARN postproc: dropped 0x200F markers in normalize_step
```
sam: I submitted a hotfix branch: kernel/keep-zwj-2026-03-14. runs with quant unit tests show token counts preserved. running overnight full eval.
eval-bot: canary run queued on dedicated pool (canary-id: canary-20260314-3).
deploy-bot: canary deployed to prod-dedicated-us-west for 2% traffic with keep-zwj flag enabled.
jin: initial canary logs look promising, korean honorific tokens preserved and vertical CJK line breaks present for 90/100 samples.
maya: great. once canary finishes, we should add a regression test: vertical-linebreaks corpus + bidi punctuation set, run on all quant levels (int8/q4) in CI.
harpreet: noted, I'll add to eng-sql that CI job and link to dataset.
jin: thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a short writeup and suggested defaults for preserve_newlines/keep_zwj. :thumbsup:
